historical_context: The Soviet counteroffensive launched 5 December 1941 — as German soldiers could see Moscow's spires — halted Operation Typhoon. It was Germany's first major strategic defeat and ended the myth of Blitzkrieg invincibility.

title: The Narrow Road to the Deep North
description: Australian surgeon Dorrigo Evans operates on dying men with no equipment, his professional identity the only thing he can maintain against the camp system's destruction of every other dignity.
historical_context: Richard Flanagan's Booker Prize-winning novel drew on his father's experience on the Death Railway. The title is from the haiku poet Bashō, giving the Pacific suffering a literary resonance beyond the historical record.

title: The Narrow Road to the Deep North
description: Evans runs an improvised hospital at the base camp, performing amputations with a saw and sutures from patients' own hair. His wartime surgery becomes the defining moral experience of his life.
historical_context: Medical officers on the Death Railway performed extraordinary improvised surgery under Japanese guards who denied adequate medical supplies as a matter of policy. POW death rates from cholera and tropical diseases were catastrophic.

title: The People vs Fritz Bauer
description: Hessian Attorney General Fritz Bauer pursues Eichmann and other war criminals in 1950s West Germany — a state where former Nazis fill the judiciary and police, and where his own office may be compromised.
historical_context: Fritz Bauer (1903–1968) was instrumental in both the Eichmann capture — he tipped off Israeli intelligence — and the Frankfurt Auschwitz trials (1963–65). He was a Jewish gay man in a hostile postwar Germany.

title: The People vs Fritz Bauer
description: Bauer passes Eichmann's location in Buenos Aires to the Israeli Mossad — bypassing his own compromised West German state — in secret because he fears tipping off Nazi networks within the German justice system.
historical_context: Bauer's tip to Israel in 1957 was treasonous under West German law — sharing intelligence with a foreign power. He knew that routing it through official channels would warn Eichmann's protectors. He never publicly disclosed his role.

title: The Plot Against America
description: In the alt-history America of Philip Roth's novel, President Charles Lindbergh governs from Washington while pursuing a policy of antisemitic persecution — the Levin family's Newark nightmare reflected in national politics.
historical_context: Charles Lindbergh was a genuine pre-war antisemite and isolationist who said Jews were 'pressing this country toward war'. Roth's novel asks: what if the most capable American Nazi had won the 1940 election?

title: The Plot Against America
description: The Lindbergh government's 'Just Folks' programme relocates urban Jewish children to rural American communities for the summer — a domestication scheme the Levin family recognises as the beginning of dispersal.
historical_context: Roth modelled 'Just Folks' on real New Deal rural programmes but gave it a sinister integrationist purpose. The series uses specific mid-century American anxiety to ask how fascism could arrive in a democracy.

title: The Warrior's Heart
description: A WWII veteran recalls his experience at Guadalcanal — one of the war's most brutal Pacific campaigns — in flashback sequences that contextualise the contemporary soldier's own experience of combat trauma.
historical_context: The Guadalcanal Campaign (August 1942 – February 1943) was the first major Allied offensive in the Pacific. Six months of fighting in jungle, heat, and disease killed 7,100 Americans and at least 19,000 Japanese.

title: The Warrior's Heart
description: The film uses the USS Arizona Memorial and Pearl Harbor as an anchor for the WWII veteran's experience — the moment that brought the United States into the war and defined a generation of American warriors.
historical_context: The USS Arizona Memorial marks the sunken hull of the battleship, which still holds the remains of 900 sailors. Over 1.8 million visitors per year come to the site, which was attacked on 7 December 1941.
